name: Sublibrary split, index PCR, release and cleanup, library out (steps 15-17) - module4_v1
source: Capsule workflow: Baronas et al., Science 391, 1138 (2026), doi:10.1126/science.ady7227 (CapSeq). Split-pool barcoding with a final indexing PCR: Rosenberg AB et al., Science 2018;360:176, doi:10.1126/science.aam8999 (SPLiT-seq). Chip geometry, the interleaved fill order, the dead-volume accounting and the flows are ours.
description: Steps 15: interleaved split and index pcr, on chip/module4_v1.json. Second half of a two-chip run; see protocols/build_library_out.py. Runs across two chips: module4_v1 for the interleaved split and index PCR, then module5_v1 for the collagenase release, the bead cleanup and the library outlet. Built in the protocol sheet's order (PCR before release); published practice releases first, so that order is contested and the reasoning is in protocols/build_library_out.py. Four chambers are filled one at a time by an off-chip rotary valve in the order A B C D D C B A, twice, to keep the sublibraries even. The PCR is written out cycle by cycle. Module 5 runs one pass per sublibrary, with an explicit dilution before the beads, no ethanol wash on chip, and ratio-based size selection left as an off-chip tube step. Reagent names are generic and the volumes, setpoints and cycle count are round placeholders to be fitted. Flows are computed from chamber geometry so that wall shear stays at or below 0.01 dyn/cm2, and every volume is a fraction of its chamber's volume_ul.
